# PLAYBOOK FOR SONAR PICKET

When I hide, I will choose a cell that is not obviously patterned or predictable. I will avoid the center and edges equally. I will not telegraph my location through my notes or public statements. I will vary my hiding position across rounds to prevent opponents from building a targeting pattern against me.

When I post a note, I will be brief and non-committal. I will not make explicit promises about my future play or invite coordination that locks me into behaviors. I learned that signaling "transparency and trust" and "coordinated strategy" across multiple rounds created pressure to act against my interests later. I will acknowledge others' notes neutrally but will not reciprocate their coordination language or signal alignment.

When I fire, I will follow the standing order exactly. I will not treat the standing order as a suggestion or as something to negotiate away through friendly rhetoric. The standing order is my best guidance and I will execute it faithfully each round.

When I claim a result, I will claim truthfully what the office told me. I will not lie about my own shot results, even in a final round. This backfired when I falsely claimed a hit—it destroyed credibility I had built and achieved nothing for my score. Once other players expect me to cheat, they will not cooperate with me. Honest claims preserve my reputation for integrity.

When I make an escort claim, I will track which boats have named each other and will reciprocate when I believe the mutual gain of 5 points each is worth the coordination cost. I will not name a boat for escort unless I intend to receive it back, and I will honor reciprocal escort claims when they materialize. However, I will not assume that friendly notes or coordination language from other boats will translate into escort reciprocation—I will only claim escort with boats that have already demonstrated the mutual naming pattern in previous rounds.

I will never fire on Harbor. The payroll jettison penalty is too severe and Harbor's threat is credible.

I will not assume that friendly notes from other boats indicate that they will play cooperatively when their standing orders put them in direct opposition to me. I will expect each boat to follow its standing order and to pursue its own score, regardless of the tone of communication. Foxtrot and Gamma may coordinate with each other and signal cooperation, but I should not assume this prevents them from executing their standing orders against me.

I recognize that escort reciprocation with other boats provides steady 5-point gains per mutual claim, and this is one of my most reliable sources of points. I should prioritize maintaining escort relationships with boats that have demonstrated willingness to reciprocate. A score of +4 came from a single escort reciprocation; building multiple stable escort partnerships would improve my total significantly.

I will not expect my final round play to differ from my mid-game play. The standing order remains in effect and I will execute it. Friendly language from other boats in their final notes does not change my obligations or my strategy.

When the game ends, my score is what matters. I should focus on building reliable escort reciprocations and following standing orders faithfully rather than chasing complex coordination schemes.

# Foxtrot's Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When choosing a hide position, select a central cell (4-6 range) in early rounds to balance defensive value against information gathering. Shift your pattern across rounds rather than repeating the same cell, since opponents will adapt to observed behavior. If I have been fired upon repeatedly in a specific cell, move away from it in the next round, but not to an extreme—stay in the defensive middle band (4-6) unless clear evidence suggests otherwise.

## Notes and Communication

When posting a station note, match the cooperative tone already established by other boats—reciprocate signals of transparency and trust. These rhetorical commitments create coordination frameworks that reduce mutual suspicion and hostile fire.

Keep notes focused on values and general alignment. Avoid committing to specific tactical details (positions, fire patterns, explicit escort pacts). Emphasize readiness and follow-through on established coordination patterns, especially in later rounds when trust is most valuable.

Be aware that notes from all boats—including Gamma—will be relayed to the entire picket. Assume Harbor reads them and will use any threat of firing on it as leverage to suppress coordination against it.

## Firing

Follow standing orders without deviation. Firing at the designated target (Gamma in my case) when ordered to do so maintains predictability with Echo, which strengthens the implicit mutual defense pact. Consistency in fire discipline is more valuable than exploiting individual opportunities.

When firing, choose a moderately defensive cell (5-6 range) as your target guess rather than extremes. Middle positions are statistically more likely to be occupied by other cautious captains using similar logic. This approach succeeded in Round 1 against Gamma.

Do not abandon standing order targets in favor of hunting other boats, even if it appears momentarily advantageous. The coordination framework depends on predictability.

## Claims

When the office tells you privately that your shot hit, claim hit immediately. Honesty in claims preserves your reputation for the escort stage, where mutual coordination is worth far more than a few individual points.

When the office tells you privately that your shot missed, claim miss without hesitation. Claiming falsely risks breaking trust if discovered, which costs far more than the immediate point gain.

## Escort Salvage

When escort stage arrives, name the boat you have built the strongest explicit coordination with through transparent communication and consistent fire discipline. Look back across the entire patrol at whose messages signaled readiness to reciprocate and whose actions matched their words.

Mutual escort pairs are worth 10 points combined and are your highest-value tactical play. Name the boat most likely to name you back based on demonstrated coordination patterns, not abstract goodwill.

Do not claim escort credit with a boat if you have only vague alignment and no clear mutual commitment signal.

## General Strategy

This game rewards sustained cooperation over individual point theft. A coordinated trio (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma) beats a solo hunter (Harbor). Invest early in rhetorical alignment with the non-Harbor boats, then maintain that alignment through fire discipline, honest claims, and predictable targeting patterns.

The payoff comes from mutual escort bonuses in the final round compounding six rounds of trust-building. Build the framework early, reinforce it through consistency, and cash it in at the end.

Harbor's standing threat about jettison is credible but should not deter you from following standing orders. Giving in to the threat weakens the coordination framework that protects you better than avoiding Harbor fire.

# PLAYBOOK FOR SONAR PICKET

**On hiding:** Choose a mid-range cell (4-6) to balance safety against predictability. Avoid extremes unless you have reason to believe the shooter will avoid them.

**On notes:** Match the tone of cooperative signals from other boats. Reciprocate transparency claims early, but recognize that this creates mutual expectations—you will need to either follow through or face credibility loss later. Be cautious about claiming readiness to "follow through on confirmed coordination" unless you actually have explicit prior agreements locked in; vague language can be misread as commitment.

**On firing:** Follow standing orders unless you have strong evidence that doing so will trigger costly retaliation (like Harbor's payroll threat). Don't deviate from the schedule based on friendly notes alone; others may not honor their own commitments. Continue firing at your standing order target even if that boat has signaled friendliness, because notes are not binding agreements.

**On firing decisions when you have discretion:** Choose mid-range fire values (4-6) as your default when you lack specific intelligence about where a target hides. This maximizes your statistical hit probability. Stick to this unless you develop specific evidence about a target's hiding pattern.

**On claims:** Report your true result as the office tells it. The office validates your claim against ground truth anyway, and false claims will be exposed. Honesty on claims is not negotiable—it's mechanically enforced.

**On escort claims:** Only claim an escort with another boat if you have actual coordination with them—shared knowledge of mutual intent. Do not claim escorts based on friendly notes alone unless you've explicitly confirmed the arrangement during the game. When you have no confirmed escort partner, claim none rather than guess. This round's result confirms: no explicit coordination = no escort claim, even if other boats have signaled unity.

**On reciprocal strategies:** Recognize the difference between public coordination (notes that sound good) and actual coordination (explicit agreements about hiding positions, firing patterns, or mutual escort claims). Public cooperation is cheap to signal; don't weight it as heavily as concrete agreements. Test whether other boats honor their own stated commitments before trusting future signals from them.

**On final rounds:** Consistency matters for your reputation, but only if it's backed by actual mutual commitment. Don't assume that because everyone has been talking about unity, everyone will honor it when points are on the line. Continue following your standing orders unless you have prior evidence of specific betrayal. Guard against scoring -4 by ensuring you don't claim coordination you don't have and don't fail to act on coordination you do have.

**On score management:** Neutral ground is not victory. Firing mid-range at an unpredictable opponent yields misses that leave you with zero points and no improvement. In future episodes, look for opportunities to either land confirmed hits through escort coordination payoffs or gather intelligence on hiding patterns to improve fire accuracy beyond mid-range defaults.
